The Go vulnerability database lists golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm Form.Append, Form.AppendString, Form.Bytes, Form.FirstBoundary, Form.FirstBoundaryInString, Form.IsNormal, Form.IsNormalString, Form.LastBoundary, Form.NextBoundary, Form.NextBoundaryInString, Form.Properties, Form.PropertiesString, Form.QuickSpan, Form.QuickSpanString, Form.Span, Form.SpanString, Form.String, Form.Transform, Iter.Init, Iter.InitString, Iter.Next, Iter.Seek, nextComposed, normReader.Read and normWriter.Write. We downloaded every build-dev package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: 91 versions from 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only, and checked each download against the index checksum. 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times per architecture with different checksums; the copy the repository serves was the one read. No package contains a symbolic link. Each package holds one program, /usr/bin/build, a Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0. We read the function table (pclntab) and build information of every Go program in every build, and searched the bytes of every ELF file in every build, which also finds the names of inlined functions; runtime.main is in the function table of every Go program. All Go programs in one build use the same Go release: 2.6.4-r0 to 2.6.6-r1 Go 1.25.7; 2.7.0-r1 to 2.8.3-r0 Go 1.25.8; 2.8.3-r1 to 2.9.2-r0 Go 1.26.1; 2.10.0-r0 to 2.15.0-r0 Go 1.26.2; 2.15.0-r1 to 2.17.3-r0 Go 1.26.3; 2.17.3-r1 to 2.20.0-r2 Go 1.26.4; 2.20.0-r3 to 2.20.0-r5 Go 1.26.5; 2.20.0-r6 Go 1.26.6; 2.20.0-r7 to 2.20.0-r10 Go 1.26.7; 2.20.0-r11 to 2.26.0-r0 Go 1.26.8; 2.26.0-r1 to 2.26.1-r0 Go 1.26.9; 2.26.1-r1 to 2.28.0-r2 Go 1.26.10; 2.28.0-r3 to 2.30.0-r0 Go 1.26.11. /usr/bin/build is built with golang.org/x/text v0.31.0 to v0.38.0 in the builds before 2.20.0-r5 and with v0.39.0 to v0.44.0 from 2.20.0-r5. From golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm, the function table of /usr/bin/build contains only the package initializer norm.init in every build, and the byte search of every ELF file in every build finds no golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm name other than norm.init, its .inittask and the nfcSparse, nfcSparseOffset, nfcSparseValues, nfkcSparse, nfkcSparseOffset and nfkcSparseValues table variables, apart from the standard library's own copy described below. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search run on a program we built with the vulnerable golang.org/x/text v0.38.0 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 that calls Iter.InitString, Iter.Next, Form.String and Form.IsNormalString find Form.IsNormalString, Form.String, Iter.InitString and nextComposed in its function table and the names golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm.(*Iter).Next and golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm.nextComposed in its bytes. The Go standard library carries its own copy of this package, vendor/golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm (from x/text v0.26.0 in Go 1.25 and v0.32.0 in Go 1.26), which is part of the standard library rather than the golang.org/x/text module this advisory covers and does not have the fix. In every Go program in every build, that copy's Form.Bytes, Form.IsNormalString, Form.String and nextComposed are in the function table, and Form.QuickSpan appears in the bytes as an inlined name. The fix commit names nextComposed as the function that can loop; its other changes switch the existing invalid-character checks to the new representation. nextComposed is linked only because the package's form table refers to it, and it runs only through a norm.Iter: no Go program in any build has that copy's Iter.Init, Iter.InitString, Iter.Next or Iter.Seek in its function table or its bytes. In the standard library, only the IDNA package (vendor/golang.org/x/net/idna) imports that copy, and it calls only Form.String, Form.Bytes, Form.QuickSpan and Form.IsNormalString, never an Iter. In a test with golang.org/x/text v0.32.0, an Iter over the truncated sequence F3 CC 80 did not finish within a two-second limit, while Form.String, Form.Bytes, Form.QuickSpan and Form.IsNormalString on 200,000 generated inputs with invalid and truncated UTF-8, and the IDNA Lookup and Punycode profiles of the golang.org/x/net version that Go 1.26.11 vendors on 300,000, always returned within it.
